then if I get involved, you know, I
could potentially get arrested. And then
I could potentially not be there the
next time something like that happened.
I'm just supposed to be the eyes for
people who can't be there. For example,
like from 26 Federal Plaza, again, two
of the floors at 26 Federal Plaza are
where there are immigration courts. So,
all last summer and into the fall, ICE
was super active waiting outside the
immigration courts and grabbing people
as they come out of the court after
they've seen the judge. The judge would
say, "Okay, we're going to continue with
your asylum claim. Come back in 2 years
with your proof." You know, they'd walk
out of the courthouse and boom,
the ICE would grab them. And there was a
lot of family separations and especially
with the family separations were really
hard to witness and really hard to
photograph, you know? You're like
photographing and crying at the same
time.
But uh you're still keeping the camera
up to your face because you That's your
job because if you don't show it, who's
going to know about it? You can explain
it, but it's not nearly as powerful
than if you see it. You see the pain in
these people's faces, then the people
who weren't there can really relate to
that. They can relate They can recognize
the pain and they can relate to it.
Because then the idea is that that
you're going to do that to show be the
proof of what's happening and galvanize
people to try to make a change.
And there has been change since there's
been so much documentation
of what's going on at 26 Federal Plaza.
You know, now
ICE is not even allowed to do arrests
there anymore. And I don't think that
change would have happened had there not
been all this documentation of what was
going on.

we're missing out on that in this day

born that way and I'll die that way. I

Right? You have that feeling like I'm in

when you get a good photo.

there's nothing better in the world,

I even dream about taking photos. Like,

fantastic
situations
and I'll be like taking photos, and

had.
>> All right, that's going to do it for
this episode of Walkie Talkie.
Stephanie, thanks for hanging out with
me today.
>> My pleasure.
Thanks for hanging out with us.

stephanie keith uh s t e f f i k e i t h

PDIlNMEs-Tk.title: a day of Large Format street photography // Walkie Talkie with Jerry Pena
PDIlNMEs-Tk.description:
Welcome to the 6th installment of my 'Walkie Talkie' series. If you're new here, I walk with a fair amount of photographers here in NYC and like to mic them up to share some of our conversation with you all. 

SUBSCRIBE to my channel if you'd like to keep seeing these pop up every week or so. 

This video features the always impressive, Jerry Pena. It's a long one, so sit back and enjoy watching Jerry lug around his large format camera & take street portraits in Manhattan. 

Show Jerry some love over on his Instagram: 
https://www.instagram.com/jerrypena_/

also here's my IG page, would love to see you there as well: 
https://www.instagram.com/paulie.b/


--
#streetphotography #nyc

eaw820DKBN0.title: Taking and Talking Street Photos in Soho & Williamsburg // Walkie Talkie with Alex Brown
eaw820DKBN0.description:
This episode was filmed last October (2021) and I finally got around to editing it. Hope you enjoy our conversation on this overcast autumn day. Consider sharing this video to your friends & parents. 

Thanks to Alex for allowing me to strap a mic on him and record every breath for a couple of hours. Please go show him some love over on his IG: 
https://instagram.com/alexskbrown
https://instagram.com/alexskbrown
https://instagram.com/alexskbrown

Support the efforts by Subscribing the channel if you're not already. It's free fast and could maybe be fun. 


Here's my IG too if you want to see more of my photos: 
https://instagram.com/paulie.b
https://instagram.com/paulie.b


--
